3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit land measuring about 96 decimals appertaining to CS Khatian 212 and SA Khatian 507 was owned and possessed by the defendant No.1 and his brother Sudhir Chandra now deceased. They transferred the said land by registered deed of sale on 14-5-1969 to the defendant No.2, Parul Bala. On 4-2-1970 Parul Bala transferred the suit land to one Sufia Khatun and delivered possession. The latter got her name recorded in the RS Khatian and possessed the suit land till she transferred it to Shahabuddin on 9-12-1977 and delivered possession. Thereafter, Shahabuddin transferred the land to the plaintiffs who now possessing the same on raising dwelling houses and mutating their names and paying rents. 

 13. He lastly submits that the learned Single Judge acted illegally in exercise of his revisional jurisdiction to set aside the finding of facts arrived at by the lower appellate Court in respect of the possession of the suit land misreading the report of the Advocate Commissioner who made a report to the effect that the major portion of the suit land was lying vacant proving the case of the defendant No.1 who is also a recorded tenant in the RS Khatian.
